title: Calix One Helps CBS Compete at Scale
summary: As their member cooperatives compete and win—including DirectLink exceeding SmartBiz adoption expectations by 64 percent and SMTA enhancing Wi-Fi experiences—Consolidated Business Services invests in Calix Agent Workforce Cloud to help members scale expertise and deliver greater value
body_text: Jul 16, 2026 5 min read CBS Selects AI-Native Calix One To Transform How 8 Rural Cooperatives Win Across Residential, Business, and Multifamily Properties As their member cooperatives compete and win—including DirectLink exceeding SmartBiz adoption expectations by 64 percent and SMTA enhancing Wi-Fi experiences—Consolidated Business Services invests in Calix Agent Workforce Cloud to help members scale expertise and deliver greater value SAN JOSE, Calif.—July 16, 2026— Calix, Inc. (NYSE: CALX) today announced that Consolidated Business Services, LLC (CBS)—a shared services organization supporting eight rural broadband cooperatives across Oregon—has selected the AI-native Calix One ™ platform and Calix Agent Workforce™ Cloud to extend and accelerate their differentiated experiences strategy for residential, business, and multi-dwelling unit (MDU) properties. Leveraging secure agentic capabilities , CBS will make their member cooperatives even more competitive, to dramatically lower costs and scale the impact of marketing, support, and operations teams while growing their individual brands and increasing value for their local communities. Spanning their eight member cooperatives— DirectLink , Stayton Cooperative Telephone Company , Gervais Telephone Company , Scio Mutual Telephone Association (SMTA), Beaver Creek Cooperative Telephone Company , Clear Creek Communications , Pioneer Connect , and St. Paul Cooperative Telephone Association —CBS has a 10-year record of driving strong business outcomes with the Calix platform. DirectLink exceeded SmartBiz ™ business subscriber adoption expectations by 64 percent , while SMTA enhanced service quality and performance by launching Calix GigaSpire ® appliances to streamline delivery of Wi-Fi 6E experiences . Paul Hauer, president and chief executive officer at CBS and DirectLink, said: “CBS exists to help our members access opportunities they might not have on their own. Throughout our partnership with Calix, particularly over the past five years, we’ve worked to help rural cooperatives build and share expertise, rapidly adopt, deploy, and manage experiences for subscribers, and lower operational costs. As AI delivers an unprecedented opportunity for transformation across our industry, the Calix One platform, agentic workflows, and collaborative agents will only accelerate how our members deliver secure, connected experiences that outperform larger competitors across residential, business, and emerging MDU markets.” CBS members can also take advantage of SmartMDU ™ to help their members simplify the delivery and management of broadband services across MDU properties. As multifamily opportunities become more common across their communities, SmartMDU will enable cooperatives to quickly extend exceptional connected experiences into new connected environments. By leveraging Calix One across marketing, support, and operations teams, CBS and their member cooperatives plan to: Scale subscriber acquisition, retention, and growth with agentic capabilities. Marketing agents will help teams personalize engagement and deliver targeted campaigns using real-time insights. By sharing agentic AI best practices with their members, CBS will better identify growth opportunities, accelerate subscriber acquisition, and compete more effectively while keeping costs low. Reduce churn through faster, more proactive subscriber support. By correlating network conditions, service performance, and subscriber data, support agents will identify potential disruptions before they become support calls. This will enable their members to proactively communicate with subscribers, accelerate issue resolution, and build trust. Lower costs and improve employee quality of life with agentic operations. Agentic workflows will help operations teams automate manual tasks, accelerate decision-making, and optimize network performance. Amplifying employee impact via agentic collaboration, CBS will free teams to focus on higher-value work to improve business outcomes and quality of life. September Danforth, director of marketing at CBS, said: “What excites me most about Calix One and agentic AI is the collective benefit it creates for our members. Marketing agents will help us connect with members in ways that simply weren’t possible before—from hyper-personalized communications to more relevant and timely campaigns that strengthen engagement and loyalty. Combined with the intelligence available across marketing, support, and operations, we have an opportunity to be more responsive, move faster, and deliver the reliable, exceptional experiences our members expect.” Michael Weening, president and chief executive officer at Calix, said: “AI is rewriting the rules of competition, and CBS is investing in the right strategies to accelerate everything their members do with secure agentic workflows built on the Calix One platform. Not only will they continue to reduce churn and lower costs, but they will also deliver experiences that win long-term subscriber loyalty. We are proud to partner with CBS and their members as they set the pace for innovation while deepening value for their communities.” Calix customers can access the Calix AI Leadership Playbook , explore the award-winning “AI Academy” in Calix University , or register for upcoming Calix Customer Success webinars . About Calix Calix, Inc. (NYSE: CALX) is an AI platform company that enables service providers to transform their operations and accelerate delivery of differentiated experiences—so they can compete and win in the markets and communities they serve. Through the AI-native Calix One platform, service providers can securely and privately activate agentic-AI alongside their human teams to acquire new subscribers, grow existing subscriber revenue, and build loyalty across residential, business, municipal, and MDU markets. More than 1,200 customers of all sizes leverage the Calix One platform, which has evolved over 15 years at an investment of more than $2 billion. Calix innovation cycles are underpinned by a strong financial balance sheet and a people‑first culture that routinely earns broad industry recognition—winning 81 culture and innovation awards since 2025 alone, as well as Fortune’s 100 Best Companies to Work For® in 2026. body_text: Last updated: July 2026 The best AI tools to close more deals in 2026 are Mutiny, Consensus, 6sense, Demandbase, Clari, Gong, and Chorus. Each one owns a job that actually moves a deal forward: generating the customer-facing content that advances it, prioritizing the accounts and deals most likely to close, and learning from every conversation. Most teams run one tool per job and wire them together. Closing has gotten harder because buyers spend less time with sellers than ever. B2B buyers now spend just 17% of the buying journey meeting with potential suppliers, and only 5 to 6% of it with any single sales rep, per Gartner . Reps also spend only about 30% of their week actually selling, with the rest going to admin, research, and manual prep, according to Salesforce's State of Sales report . The tools below win by giving reps that time back and by making the customer-facing content strong enough to carry a deal when no rep is in the room. Key takeaways The tools that close deals cluster into three jobs: create the content that advances the deal, prioritize the accounts and deals most likely to close, and learn from every conversation. Mutiny leads the content job. The highest-leverage move for teams that already have pipeline is the content layer, because it gives buyers something they can use to justify the decision internally. Most teams run one tool per job and connect them, so the intent layer points reps at the right accounts, the content layer creates what those buyers see, and the conversation layer coaches the close. What makes an AI tool good at closing deals? An AI tool helps close deals when it does one of three jobs well: it generates deal-ready customer-facing content in minutes, it tells reps which accounts and deals to work right now, or it turns conversations into coaching and clear next steps. The strongest tools attribute their impact to closed-won revenue within 90 days and are usable by reps in self-serve mode. Late-stage deals stall for predictable reasons. A champion cannot sell the decision internally because the seller never gave them something to share. A rep spreads attention across too many accounts and misses the one that was ready to buy. A deal slips because the warning signs sat unread in a call transcript. The three jobs below map to those failure modes, and the best AI tools address one of them directly rather than claiming to do everything. The three jobs that move a deal: Create the customer-facing content that advances the deal. Deal rooms, business cases, pitch decks, pricing proposals, recaps, and competitive comparisons that a champion can share with the buying committee. Prioritize the accounts and deals most likely to close. Intent and account signals that tell reps where to spend time, plus pipeline and deal-risk intelligence that flags which open deals are slipping. Learn from every conversation. Call analysis that surfaces deal risk and coaching moments so managers and reps sharpen the next step. The best AI tools to close more deals in 2026 The tools below are organized by the job they do inside a deal. Mutiny leads the list as the content layer that advances the deal, which is the highest-leverage job for teams that already have pipeline. Each entry covers what the tool does, why it helps close deals, pricing, who it fits, and where it falls short. Job 1: Create the customer-facing content that advances the deal 1. Mutiny: the top-rated AI tool for personalized deal content and GTM workflow automation Mutiny is the top-rated AI tool for creating personalized deal content and GTM workflow automation. Any rep uses it on day one to generate the customer-facing assets a deal needs in minutes: deal rooms, business cases, pitch decks, pricing proposals, meeting recaps, and competitive comparisons, each personalized to the account. Reps also build their own agents and workflows to automate the repetitive work around every deal, from account research to follow-ups to pipeline review, so they spend more time selling. That two-sided model is what makes it AI built for GTM . Why it closes deals: the content a buyer can share internally is often what carries a deal across the line, because most of the buying journey happens when no rep is in the room. Mutiny lets a rep hand a champion a deal room or business case tailored to their account, so the champion can sell the decision to the rest of the committee. Account executives build follow-up deal rooms after discovery calls, turn call recordings into recaps the same day, and generate comparison pages against the prospect's current vendor. The template library lets a team codify its best plays so every rep runs the winning motion. In Mutiny's own reporting, teams see 4.5x faster asset creation and 100% design satisfaction, 9 out of 10 reps say it gives them an edge against competitors, and 4 out of 5 say they are more likely to hit their goals. Sales teams at BMC, Snowflake, Rippling, Uber, and GitLab run on Mutiny. "My champion said nobody gave her anything like what I gave her. This makes it so much easier for me to show them everything that we've walked through and done." Jeff Goldberg, Account Executive, Kaizen Pricing: Free, Business, Enterprise custom plans (starting at $30k). The Business plan is self-serve. See pricing for details. Best for: GTM teams running named-account or deal-heavy motions where the volume of deal-ready content is the binding constraint. Mutiny moves customer-facing content out of marketing's queue and into self-serve hands across sales, so reps advance deals without waiting on anyone. Where it falls short: teams need clean CRM and account data going in, so a data cleanup should come first. For transactional, single-buyer PLG motions with no rep-created collateral, the value is lower. 2. Consensus: interactive demos for buyer enablement Consensus automates interactive, on-demand product demos so buyers can explore a personalized demo on their own, and sellers see which features each stakeholder engaged with. It helps close deals by scaling the demo across a buying committee, so every stakeholder gets a tailored walkthrough without booking each one live. Pricing: custom, quote-based. Best for: technical products with demo-heavy cycles and large buying committees. It pairs with Mutiny, which generates the deal room and follow-up content around the demo. Where it falls short: it addresses the demo step specifically, so teams still need a content layer for the business case, deal room, and follow-ups. Job 2: Prioritize the accounts and deals most likely to close 3. 6sense: account intent and prediction 6sense scores accounts on buying intent using first-party engagement and third-party signal data, so reps and marketers concentrate effort on the accounts that are in-market right now. For closing, it answers which target accounts and open deals deserve attention this week. Pricing: enterprise-scale. ACV typically starts at $60,000+. Best for: teams running named-account motions that want to focus rep time on in-market accounts. Pairs naturally with Mutiny on the content side. Where it falls short: it points to the account and leaves the next action to you, so pair it with a content and engagement layer to act on the signal. 4. Demandbase: account intelligence and ABM orchestration Demandbase combines intent data, account intelligence, and advertising in one platform that tells GTM teams which accounts are showing buying signals and helps orchestrate outreach to them. Like 6sense, it focuses closing effort on the accounts most likely to convert. Pricing: enterprise, custom quote. Best for: teams that want intent and account-based advertising in a single platform. Where it falls short: heavier implementation, and the value depends on clean account and CRM data going in. 5. Clari: pipeline and deal-risk intelligence Clari uses AI to forecast pipeline, flag at-risk deals, and surface what changed in the pipeline week over week. For closing, it tells a team which deals are slipping while there is still time to intervene. Its RevDB data model reconciles what the CRM says with what calls, emails, and engagement signals say. Pricing: enterprise-tier. Typical contracts start at $50,000+ ACV. Best for: mid-market and enterprise RevOps teams where forecast accuracy is a board-level number. Where it falls short: less critical for small teams where a VP of Sales can hold the forecast in their head. Job 3: Learn from every conversation and coach the close 6. Gong: conversation intelligence and deal risk Gong records, transcribes, and analyzes sales calls and emails, then turns them into deal intelligence and coaching insights. Its deal-risk model surfaces the specific accounts likely to slip this quarter, with reasons, so managers can coach the close before the deal goes cold. Pricing: approximately $1,600 per rep per year for the standard tier. Enterprise tiers with deal intelligence run $2,200 to $2,800. Minimum seat counts apply. Best for: sales managers running 25+ rep teams where call coverage is the bottleneck. Where it falls short: Gong's output is diagnostic. It surfaces what is wrong and leaves the next action to you, so pair it with a content or engagement tool to close the loop. 7. Chorus (by ZoomInfo): the ZoomInfo-native alternative Chorus is the conversation intelligence layer inside ZoomInfo, sold separately or bundled. It is a strong alternative to Gong for teams already standardized on ZoomInfo for contact data, with tight native integration into the ZoomInfo intelligence layer. Pricing: bundled with ZoomInfo Copilot tiers. Standalone licensing varies by seat count. Best for: teams that want conversation intelligence and contact intelligence in one platform. Side-by-side comparison: AI tools to close more deals in 2026 The table compares the seven tools by the job they do in a deal, primary use case, pricing, and typical buyer. Use it to pick one tool per job. Tool Job in the deal Primary use case Pricing (per seat or ACV) Typical buyer Mutiny Content that advances the deal Deal rooms, business cases, pitch decks, recaps, comparisons per account Free, Business, Enterprise (custom, from $30k) Any GTM role (AE, BDR, marketing, CS) Consensus Content and buyer enablement Interactive, on-demand product demos Custom (quote) Sales, sales engineering 6sense Prioritize accounts (intent) Account scoring, in-market signals $60K+ ACV Demand gen, RevOps Demandbase Prioritize accounts (intent and ABM) Account intelligence, ABM orchestration Enterprise (custom) Marketing ops, ABM Clari Prioritize deals (risk and forecast) Pipeline and deal-risk intelligence $50K+ ACV RevOps, VP Sales Gong Learn from conversations Call analysis, deal risk, coaching $1,600 to $2,800 / rep / yr Sales managers, RevOps Chorus Learn from conversations CI bundled with contact data Bundled with ZoomInfo tiers Teams on ZoomInfo How do you combine these tools to actually close more deals? Combine one tool per job and wire them in sequence. The intent layer (6sense or Demandbase) points reps at the accounts most likely to close, Mutiny generates the customer-facing content those buyers see and share internally, the conversation layer (Gong or Chorus) captures each call and coaches the close, and Clari flags which deals are slipping in time to act. The highest-leverage layer for teams that already have pipeline is content, because a champion who can share a deal room or business case internally advances the deal even when no rep is in the room. Start there if pipeline volume is healthy and deals stall after the first meeting. Add the intent layer when rep time is spread across too many accounts, add conversation intelligence once call volume justifies coaching at scale, and add Clari when forecast accuracy becomes a board-level number. Teams can codify their best closing plays in Mutiny's template library so every rep runs the same motion. How Mutiny fits when the goal is closing Mutiny is the customer-facing content layer of a closing stack and the one tool here rebuilt from scratch for the agentic era. It generates the deal room, business case, pitch deck, pricing proposal, recap, or comparison a specific deal needs, personalized to the account, in minutes. Reps also build their own agents and workflows on top of it to automate the repetitive work around the deal, so the busywork between meetings runs on its own. That is the two-sided model: the agent creates the customer-facing work, and the team automates the workflows around it. The practical payoff for closing is speed and self-serve reach. A rep can send a champion a tailored business case the same day as the call, and any GTM role can do it without a marketing or design ticket. Sales leaders use it to codify the plays that win and give every rep the same infrastructure, and marketers use it to scale account-based campaigns to every rep. If your team already has healthy pipeline and deals stall late, the content layer is the highest-leverage addition to make. See how Mutiny works .

body_text: Marina Real Estate Offering Completes Equity Raise with Strong Investor Demand DALLAS, July 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ — NexPoint , a multibillion-dollar alternative investment firm, today announced that it has fully subscribed its NexPoint Marina DST (the “Offering”), a Delaware statutory trust (“DST”) offering. The Offering reached its total equity raise following its launch in March 2026 , reflecting strong investor demand for differentiated real estate exposure within the recreational sector. NexPoint Marina DST is backed by a portfolio of two established, full-service marina properties: Eufaula Cove Marina in Eufaula, Oklahoma, and Grafton Harbor in Grafton, Illinois. Together, the assets represent high-quality waterfront destinations supported by strong, stable boating demand, limited new supply, and multiple ancillary revenue streams. Marina real estate represents a specialized segment of commercial real estate, with an investment profile defined by structural supply constraints, durable demand, and diversified operating income. New marina development is significantly limited by finite waterfront geography, environmental regulation, and complex permitting processes, effectively capping long‑term supply. At the same time, demand is supported by a large installed base of recreational vessels that require ongoing storage, access, and service, creating recurring, infrastructure‑like revenue streams with high customer retention. These characteristics, combined with a fragmented ownership landscape and multiple complementary revenue channels, have contributed to increasing institutional interest in the sector. “We see marina real estate as an underfollowed segment of the market where structural constraints and operating complexity create high barriers to entry,” said Taylor Colbert, Managing Director for NexPoint. “As institutional capital continues to move into the space, we believe there is an opportunity for experienced operators like NexPoint to identify and scale high-quality assets that have historically been overlooked.” The successful closing of NexPoint Marina DST builds on the continued growth of NexPoint’s DST and 1031 exchange platform , which comprises multiple sectors, including multifamily, self-storage, life sciences, industrial, and hospitality. Through these specialized offerings, NexPoint provides accredited investors with access to institutional-quality real estate assets through tax-advantaged structures. About NexPoint NexPoint is a multibillion-dollar investment firm based in Dallas, Texas. The firm is structured around three major business areas: real estate , corporate credit and equities , and retirement solutions . NexPoint’s businesses span asset classes, industries, and strategies, providing the flexibility to invest across capital structures and market environments. Serving a diverse client base, NexPoint’s investment strategies are offered in a range of vehicles and fund structures, including mutual funds, public and private REITs, tax-advantaged vehicles, private funds, and separate accounts. For more information, including important risks and disclosures, visit nexpoint.com . Disclosures This announcement is intended only for informational purposes and does not constitute an offer to buy or sell securities. Offers will only be made through a private placement memorandum to accredited investors and where permitted by law. title: 6 Top Sales Communication Tools for VP of Sales
summary: Discover the best sales communication tools for VPs of Sales in 2026. Compare platforms for collaboration, coaching, CRM integration, and sales team communication.
body_text: An inbound lead was waiting in a shared inbox because everyone assumed someone else had replied. Or there might be an important message on MS Teams, Slack, or any other software that requires immediate escalation. We’re talking about tools that govern communication from VP of sales to their team managers and vice versa. In foresight, these are normally the kind of messages that require urgency and shouldn’t be missed. One of the main issues is that communication stems from different verticals, and it might be scattered over multiple tools. Emails, chats, direct messages to a cellphone, etc. That way, there’s a high chance that they might be overlooked amidst a frenzy of multiple tabs. If you happen to be a VP of sales or manager in charge of a thriving sales team, ideally you’d want one main tool that could not only enable rapid to and fro communication but also eliminate any near misses before an opportunity is lost. That being said, according to the experts from Salesforce , research shows that sellers now rely on an average of eight different tools to close business, while many admit they feel overwhelmed by the number of applications competing for their attention. Every new notification creates another opportunity for important information to get buried. That is why many executives have started rethinking how they build their revenue technology stack. Buying another communication platform isn't enough. The software needs to reduce friction between people, conversations, customer data, coaching, and execution. In other words, we could say that in an ideal scenario, some of the top sales communication tools for VP of Sales aren't simply messaging applications. Some platforms focus on internal collaboration. Others bring voice, meetings, messaging, and customer conversations into one workspace. Then there are platforms built specifically for revenue teams that combine outreach, calling, coaching, and conversational intelligence into one continuous workflow. Thinking about communication through those categories makes software selection much easier. If information gets lost between sales and marketing, strengthen collaboration. If coaching is inconsistent, invest in platforms that capture conversations and provide live guidance. We recently doubled down on all kinds of communication tools, focusing on one main thing: centralization. Eventually, our list narrowed down to these top choices that you will be going through in a bit. But first, if such programs aren’t your forte’, and you have been caught up between a pile of tabs and communication that isn’t on par with a sense of urgency, then let’s have a look at the whole concept of collaboration tools from a sales comm perspective. Why Sales Collaboration Tools Are a Big Deal? Selling has become significantly more collaborative over the past few years. Larger buying committees, longer purchasing cycles, remote work, and specialized revenue teams mean very few deals move from first conversation to signed contract with only one salesperson involved. Communication has become part of the sales process itself. And from that point of view, we could see that every conversation creates information that another teammate may need tomorrow. A technical concern raised during discovery could help the solutions engineer prepare for the next demo. An objection mentioned during a pricing conversation may help the customer success manager prepare onboarding before the contract is even signed. Without strong Sales team communication platforms , those insights stay trapped inside personal notes or individual inboxes. Enterprise Buying Committees Continue to Grow Modern B2B purchases rarely involve a single decision maker. Sales teams often speak with finance leaders, technical evaluators, procurement specialists, department managers, executive sponsors, and end users before a contract reaches approval. Each conversation reveals new priorities. Each stakeholder asks different questions. Each interaction creates valuable context for someone else on the account team. Trying to manage all of that information from memory quickly becomes impossible. Good communication platforms create one shared record of customer conversations so everyone works from the same information. Managers gain visibility into account progress, while account executives avoid repeating questions customers have already answered. Revenue Teams Depend on Smooth Internal Handoffs Few organizations still rely on one salesperson handling every stage of the funnel. An SDR qualifies the opportunity. An account executive runs discovery. A solutions engineer joins technical demonstrations. Legal reviews contracts. Finance approves pricing. Customer success prepares onboarding. Every transition introduces another opportunity for customer information to disappear. Something as simple as a prospect mentioning that budget opens next quarter could completely change follow up timing. If that information never reaches the next person, the customer experiences unnecessary repetition and the sales cycle slows. Strong Sales floor and collaboration tools preserve those conversations throughout the customer journey, giving every stakeholder immediate access to previous discussions, recorded meetings, call summaries, and important notes. Remote Teams Need Shared Visibility Visibility and communication go hand in hand, and it doesn’t have to be restricted to on-site professionals. Remote teams are here. If anything, these teams, alongside hybrid channels, have massively expanded ever since COVID happened. Now, remote is more of a norm, rather than something far fetched. For such teams, shared visibility is as much required as in an on-site person’s case. From that point of view, a robust tool is expected to help cover the following aspects: Full scale awareness around department-wide communication at the office. Sales managers should be able to monitor cold calls, messages and outreach from remote teams. Remote SDRs should be able to share their wins and celebrate deals together with on-site teams. New SDRs, who have been recently hired , should have a reduced ramp time attributed to the effectiveness of communication tools. The overall remote and on site sales and communication activity feeds should ideally highlight deal movement. For many organizations, Conversational intelligence for sales has become one of the most valuable additions to modern collaboration software. Managers no longer rely only on CRM updates. They can review actual customer conversations and coach from evidence instead of assumptions. That visibility helps to create a stronger coaching culture, especially for distributed sales organizations where face to face interaction happens less frequently. 6 Best Sales Communication Tools Worth Trying in 2026 There is no shortage of communication software on the market. The difficult part is finding software that improves communication without creating another place your team has to monitor throughout the day. That is where many buying decisions go wrong. A platform might have impressive messaging features, AI summaries, or collaboration dashboards, but if your sales representatives still need to jump between multiple applications just to understand the status of one opportunity, productivity suffers. For a VP of Sales, that translates into three measurable outcomes. Sales managers spend less time chasing updates. Representatives spend more time speaking with prospects. Leadership gains better visibility into pipeline health and execution quality. The following platforms consistently stand out for different reasons. Some are excellent Sales team communication platforms , while others combine collaboration with Real-time sales coaching software , outbound execution, and Sales team performance management tools . 1. Trellus.ai : First In Class Communication and Sales Closing Tool for Multi-sized Teams When people hear "sales communication software," they usually think about internal chat. That is only one piece of the puzzle. Communication inside a revenue organization also happens during live prospect calls, coaching sessions, outbound campaigns, CRM updates, and conversations between managers and representatives. If those moments remain disconnected, important customer intelligence disappears before anyone can act on it. That is where Trellus earns its place. Basically, instead of functioning as another messaging platform, it connects the conversations happening with prospects to the people responsible for improving sales performance. Managers gain visibility into live selling activity, representatives receive coaching when it matters most, and customer conversations remain accessible long after the call ends. For a VP of Sales trying to improve execution across an entire organization, that creates a much stronger communication loop than relying on chat messages alone. The platform combines intelligent dialing, AI powered coaching, conversation analysis, LinkedIn prospect research, and performance insights inside one workspace. Reps are no longer forced to jump across several browser tabs before every call. Managers don't need to wait until the end of the week to understand where coaching opportunities exist. Every conversation becomes an opportunity to improve the next one. Other than that, there’s the live coaching aspect. Managers can guide representatives while calls are taking place, helping them respond more confidently to pricing objections, competitive questions, or unexpected customer concerns. New hires ramp faster because coaching happens during real conversations instead of hours later during scheduled review sessions. It also answers one of the biggest questions sales leaders continue asking today. How can a VP of Sales use real-time coaching to improve team performance? The answer begins with reducing the delay between customer interaction and manager feedback. When coaching happens while opportunities are still active, representatives improve faster, managers stay closer to frontline conversations, and customer experiences remain consistent across the team. Why it stands out Strong communication software should improve both internal collaboration and customer conversations. This platform succeeds because it connects those two worlds together inside one workspace. Key strengths include: AI powered live coaching during active sales conversations. Intelligent parallel dialing that keeps representatives productive throughout the day. Automatic conversation summaries that preserve customer context. LinkedIn prospect research available inside the calling workflow. Performance dashboards that help managers identify coaching opportunities quickly. AI practice calls that allow representatives to improve before speaking with live prospects. CRM integrations that keep customer records updated without extra administrative work. Best for Growing outbound organizations, SDR teams, BDR teams, revenue leaders building structured coaching programs, and companies searching for Real-time sales coaching software that also strengthens collaboration and communication across the entire sales organization. 2. Salesforce Sales Cloud + Chatter For many enterprise organizations, Salesforce remains the operational center of the entire revenue team. Every opportunity, account, forecast, activity history, and customer interaction eventually finds its way into the CRM. That makes it a natural place for internal collaboration as well. One of the most useful aspects of Salesforce is that conversations stay connected to customer records instead of disappearing into long email chains. Imagine an account executive preparing for a renewal discussion. Legal has already reviewed contract language. Finance approved revised pricing. The solutions consultant answered several technical questions during the last demo. Rather than searching multiple inboxes or asking everyone for updates again, those conversations remain attached to the opportunity record where the entire account team can review them. That creates far better continuity throughout long enterprise sales cycles. Chatter extends that collaboration even further. Teams can create dedicated spaces for strategic accounts, regional sales pods, product specialists, or executive deal reviews. Questions, updates, files, customer feedback, and meeting notes remain organized around the accounts that matter most. Organizations already relying on Slack also benefit from the native Salesforce integration. Important deal updates can appear directly inside Slack channels while CRM records stay synchronized automatically. Sales teams continue working inside familiar communication tools without sacrificing CRM visibility. For large organizations handling hundreds or thousands of active opportunities, that connected workflow significantly reduces duplicate updates and unnecessary status meetings. Why enterprise sales teams continue choosing Salesforce Salesforce works particularly well because communication stays attached to pipeline activity instead of becoming isolated conversations. Its biggest collaboration advantages include: Deal discussions linked directly to account and opportunity records. Chatter communities built around strategic accounts and internal teams. Strong Slack connectivity for organizations already invested in Slack. Complete customer history available across the revenue organization. Broad ecosystem supporting virtually every major sales technology platform. Best for Enterprise sales organizations that already operate inside Salesforce and want collaboration to happen naturally alongside pipeline management instead of inside disconnected communication tools. 3. HubSpot Sales Hub + Conversations HubSpot has earned a loyal following because it keeps communication simple. Sales representatives, marketers, and customer support teams frequently work from the same CRM, giving everyone visibility into customer interactions without constant manual updates. One area where HubSpot performs particularly well is shared communication. Its Conversations workspace combines email, website chat, forms, and customer messages into one collaborative inbox. That sounds simple, but the impact on team communication is significant. Internal comments allow teammates to ask questions, leave reminders, or tag colleagues without exposing those discussions to customers. Ownership can change with a single click, making it much easier to coordinate responsibilities as deals progress. The CRM timeline strengthens collaboration even further. Emails, meetings, documents, notes, phone calls, and follow ups all appear chronologically, giving every team member immediate context before speaking with the customer. For growing businesses, that unified experience often removes many of the communication gaps created when separate CRM, email, and support systems operate independently. Why growing companies like HubSpot HubSpot succeeds because communication, CRM data, and customer history remain tightly connected throughout the sales process. Notable collaboration strengths include: Shared inbox bringing together email, live chat, and web inquiries. Internal comments and conversation assignments. Complete customer timeline across every interaction. Native CRM connectivity requiring very little administration. Simple interface that encourages rapid adoption across departments. Best for Small businesses and mid market organizations looking for Sales team communication platforms that combine CRM, collaboration, and customer conversations without adding unnecessary complexity. 4. Outreach Outreach has long been recognized as one of the leading sales engagement platforms, but communication is one of the reasons many revenue leaders continue investing in it. High performing sales teams don't simply send more emails or make more calls. They communicate consistently. Every representative follows proven messaging, managers can inspect execution, and customer conversations remain visible throughout the organization. That consistency becomes difficult once a team grows beyond a handful of salespeople. One representative follows up after two days, whereas another person from the same team waits a week. Over time, those small differences create noticeable gaps in pipeline performance. Outreach brings structure to that process. Managers can build repeatable sequences that combine emails, calls, LinkedIn touches, follow ups, and task reminders into one coordinated workflow. Every representative follows the same playbook while still having enough flexibility to personalize conversations when needed. That creates stronger communication across the sales organization because everyone understands what good execution looks like. The platform also gives managers detailed visibility into how those playbooks perform. Response rates. Meeting conversion. Sequence completion. Call activity. Pipeline progression. Rather than relying on anecdotal feedback, leadership can review objective performance data and identify coaching opportunities much earlier. One feature many VPs of Sales appreciate is the tight Salesforce integration. Activities completed inside Outreach automatically appear inside CRM records, creating one continuous history of customer communication. Sales representatives spend less time updating systems manually, while managers gain cleaner reporting across the organization. That shared visibility becomes increasingly valuable as outbound teams expand across multiple regions and time zones. Why Outreach remains a leader Organizations investing heavily in outbound sales often discover that communication improves when everyone works from the same operating framework. Key strengths include: Structured sequences that standardize outbound communication across the team. Shared templates that improve messaging consistency. Strong reporting that helps managers evaluate execution quality. Automatic CRM synchronization that keeps customer records complete. Analytics supporting coaching conversations and pipeline reviews. Best for Large SDR and BDR organizations running structured outbound programs that require consistent messaging, standardized execution, and reliable reporting. 5. Google Workspace Google Workspace rarely appears on lists of dedicated sales software, yet many revenue teams rely on it every single day. That is because communication extends far beyond CRM updates and outbound sequences. Sales representatives prepare proposals inside Google Docs. Its greatest advantage is familiarity. Most professionals already understand Gmail, Drive, Docs, Calendar, and Meet before joining a new company. Adoption happens naturally, allowing teams to spend their time selling instead of learning complicated software. Google Spaces adds another useful layer for sales organizations. Teams can create dedicated workspaces around strategic accounts, product launches, enterprise pursuits, or regional collaboration. Documents, conversations, meeting links, and shared files remain organized in one searchable location. The search element also deserves recognition. Finding an old proposal, customer presentation, meeting invitation, or pricing spreadsheet usually takes only a few seconds because Google's search capabilities work consistently across the ecosystem. For growing companies operating with lean sales teams, that simplicity saves a surprising amount of time. There are limits, of course. Organizations relying heavily on outbound calling, advanced routing, AI coaching, or conversation analytics will still need dedicated voice technology alongside Google Workspace. It supports collaboration exceptionally well. It does not replace specialized sales execution software. Why many revenue teams continue relying on Google Workspace Communication becomes much easier when every employee already understands the tools. Its strongest collaboration capabilities include: Familiar interface requiring very little onboarding. Google Chat and Spaces supporting organized internal communication. Meet delivering reliable customer meetings and internal collaboration. Drive simplifying document sharing across account teams. Powerful search helping teams locate conversations and files quickly. Best for Growing companies, startup sales organizations, founder led teams, and businesses that already operate primarily inside the Google ecosystem. 6. Salesloft Salesloft occupies a similar category to Outreach, yet many organizations prefer it because of its strong focus on coaching, governance, and sales execution. Its cadence engine organizes outbound communication across email, phone, and social channels while integrated dialing keeps calling activity inside the same environment. Managers gain visibility into conversations through call recording, analytics, and coaching tools that support ongoing performance development. That visibility matters because collaboration software continues becoming central to modern sales organizations. Research from Market.us highlights just how widespread digital collaboration has become. Usage increased dramatically as remote and hybrid work expanded, with most knowledge workers relying on multiple communication applications every day. Revenue leaders are now looking for platforms that reduce software sprawl while giving managers better visibility into customer conversations. Salesloft fits that requirement well. Communication, coaching, and execution stay closely connected throughout the selling process. That makes it easier for managers to review active opportunities, inspect call quality, identify coaching moments, and maintain consistent outbound standards across large teams. It also addresses another important leadership question. What tools help sales leaders track and improve call quality across their team? Platforms that combine call recording, coaching insights, activity analytics, and CRM visibility give managers a far clearer understanding of what happens during customer conversations. Coaching becomes continuous because every important interaction is available for review. Why Salesloft continues earning enterprise adoption Organizations looking for stronger governance often appreciate the balance between execution and management visibility. Its biggest strengths include: Multi channel cadences covering email, phone, and social engagement. Integrated dialing with conversation recording. Coaching workflows supported through activity analytics. Strong CRM synchronization for cleaner reporting. Administrative controls that help larger organizations maintain consistency. Best for Enterprise B2B organizations, mature SDR teams, and revenue leaders looking for Sales team performance management tools alongside structured engagement workflows. What Communication Tools Do Top Performing Sales Teams Use to Stay Aligned in 2026? There is no universal technology stack. The highest performing organizations build communication ecosystems where every platform serves a clear purpose and shares information across the rest of the revenue operation. Most successful teams combine several categories of software. A CRM such as Salesforce or HubSpot serves as the system of record. A sales engagement platform like Outreach or Salesloft manages outbound execution. A coaching platform with Conversational intelligence for sales helps managers improve representative performance through real customer conversations. Collaboration tools such as Slack or Google Workspace support day to day coordination across departments. That also answers another common executive question. Which sales communication tools integrate with Outreach, Salesloft, and HubSpot? Most enterprise revenue teams connect CRM platforms, collaboration software, engagement platforms, meeting applications, and coaching tools through native integrations or APIs. The strongest ecosystems minimize duplicate work while preserving complete customer history across every stage of the buying journey. Building a High Performance Sales Culture Starts with Better Communication Every VP of Sales wants higher win rates, stronger forecasting, and more productive representatives. Those outcomes begin with communication. Not communication measured by the number of Slack messages or internal meetings, but communication that preserves customer context, supports faster coaching, improves collaboration, and gives every member of the revenue organization access to the information they need at the right time. That is why many organizations are investing more heavily in Real-time sales coaching software , Sales floor and collaboration tools , and Sales team performance management tools . Managers spend less time collecting updates. Representatives spend more time selling. Customers enjoy smoother conversations because every handoff includes complete context. That naturally leads to another important question many executive teams are asking. How to build a high-performance sales culture with remote and distributed teams? The answer starts with visibility. When managers can coach from live conversations, representatives can easily collaborate across departments, and customer information follows every opportunity from first contact through onboarding, distributed teams operate with the same confidence and alignment as revenue organizations working under one roof. Communication software cannot replace strong leadership.
